title_en: Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purpose of protecting and improving the environment, preventing and controlling pollution and other public hazards, safeguarding public health, promoting ecological civilization, and promoting sustainable economic and social development.

Article 2 For the purpose of this Law, "environment" means the aggregate of various natural and artificially modified natural factors that affect human survival and development, including the atmosphere, water, oceans, land, mineral deposits, forests, grasslands, wetlands, wildlife, natural relics, cultural relics, nature reserves, scenic spots, cities, and rural areas.
Article 3 This Law shall apply to the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China.

Article 4 Environmental protection is a basic national policy of the State.
The State shall adopt economic and technical policies and measures that are conducive to the conservation and recycling of resources, the protection and improvement of the environment, and the harmony between man and nature, so as to coordinate economic and social development with environmental protection.
Article 5 Environmental protection shall adhere to the principles of giving priority to protection, focusing on prevention, comprehensive treatment, public participation, and liability for damage.

Article 6 All units and individuals shall have the obligation to protect the environment.
Local people's governments at all levels shall be responsible for the environmental quality within their respective administrative regions.
Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and business operators shall prevent and reduce environmental pollution and ecological damage, and shall bear liability according to law for any damage caused.
Citizens shall enhance their awareness of environmental protection, adopt low-carbon and frugal lifestyles, and voluntarily fulfill their obligations to protect the environment.

Article 7 The State shall support scientific and technological research, development, and application in environmental protection, encourage the development of the environmental protection industry, promote the construction of environmental protection informatization, and improve the scientific and technological level of environmental protection.

Article 8 People's governments at all levels shall increase financial input for protecting and improving the environment and preventing and controlling pollution and other public hazards, and shall improve the efficiency of the use of financial funds.

Article 9 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen the publicity and popularization of environmental protection, encourage grassroots autonomous organizations, social organizations, and environmental protection volunteers to carry out publicity on environmental protection laws, regulations, and knowledge, and create a good atmosphere for environmental protection.
The education administrative departments and schools shall incorporate environmental protection knowledge into the content of school education and cultivate students' awareness of environmental protection.
The news media shall carry out publicity on environmental protection laws, regulations, and knowledge, and conduct public opinion supervision over illegal acts that cause environmental damage.

Article 10 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall exercise unified supervision and management over environmental protection work nationwide; the competent departments of environmental protection of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall exercise unified supervision and management over environmental protection work within their respective administrative regions.
The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level and the environmental protection departments of the armed forces shall, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, exercise supervision and management over environmental protection work such as resource conservation and pollution prevention and control.
Article 11 Units and individuals that have made remarkable achievements in protecting and improving the environment shall be rewarded by the people's government.
Article 12 June 5 of each year shall be Environmental Day.

Article 13 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate environmental protection work into their national economic and social development plans.
The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall, in conjunction with relevant departments, formulate the national environmental protection plan based on the national economic and social development plan, and submit it to the State Council for approval and promulgation for implementation.
The competent departments of environmental protection of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in conjunction with relevant departments, formulate the environmental protection plans for their respective administrative regions based on the requirements of the national environmental protection plan, and submit them to the people's governments at the same level for approval and promulgation for implementation.
The contents of environmental protection plans shall include objectives, tasks, and safeguard measures for ecological protection and pollution prevention and control, and shall be coordinated with the main functional zone plan, the overall land use plan, and the urban and rural plan.

Article 14 When organizing the formulation of economic and technical policies, the relevant departments of the State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall give full consideration to the impact on the environment and solicit opinions from relevant parties and experts.

Article 15 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall formulate national environmental quality standards.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate local environmental quality standards for items not covered by the national environmental quality standards; for items already covered by the national environmental quality standards, they may formulate local environmental quality standards that are stricter than the national environmental quality standards. Local environmental quality standards shall be reported to the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council for recordation.
The State encourages the conduct of research on environmental quality benchmarks.

Article 16 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall, based on the national environmental quality standards and the national economic and technical conditions, formulate national pollutant discharge standards.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate local pollutant discharge standards for items not covered by the national pollutant discharge standards; for items already covered by the national pollutant discharge standards, they may formulate local pollutant discharge standards that are stricter than the national pollutant discharge standards. Local pollutant discharge standards shall be reported to the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council for recordation.

Article 17 The State shall establish and improve the environmental monitoring system. The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall formulate monitoring specifications, organize monitoring networks in conjunction with relevant departments, uniformly plan the establishment of national environmental quality monitoring stations (points), establish a mechanism for sharing monitoring data, and strengthen the management of environmental monitoring.
The establishment of environmental quality monitoring stations (points) of various types, including those for relevant industries and professions, shall comply with the provisions of laws and regulations and the requirements of monitoring specifications.
Monitoring institutions shall use monitoring equipment that conforms to national standards and comply with monitoring specifications. Monitoring institutions and their responsible persons shall be responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of monitoring data.

Article 18 People's governments at or above the provincial level shall organize relevant departments or entrust professional institutions to investigate and assess the environmental situation, and establish a mechanism for monitoring and early warning of the carrying capacity of environmental resources.

Article 19 For the formulation of relevant development and utilization plans, and for the construction of projects that may have an impact on the environment, environmental impact assessment shall be conducted according to law.
Development and utilization plans that have not undergone environmental impact assessment according to law shall not be organized for implementation; construction projects that have not undergone environmental impact assessment according to law shall not be commenced.

Article 20 The State shall establish a coordinated mechanism for joint prevention and control of environmental pollution and ecological damage in key areas and river basins that cross administrative regions, and shall implement unified planning, unified standards, unified monitoring, and unified prevention and control measures.
For the prevention and control of environmental pollution and ecological damage across administrative regions other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, the superior people's government shall coordinate and resolve the matter, or the relevant local people's governments shall resolve the matter through consultation.

Article 21 The State shall adopt policies and measures in respect of finance, taxation, pricing, government procurement, and other aspects to encourage and support the development of environmental protection industries such as environmental protection technology and equipment, comprehensive utilization of resources, and environmental services.

Article 22 Where enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators, on the basis of meeting the statutory requirements for pollutant discharge, further reduce pollutant discharge, the people's government shall, according to law, adopt policies and measures in respect of finance, taxation, pricing, government procurement, and other aspects to encourage and support them.

Article 23 Where enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators convert to other production, relocate, or close down for the purpose of improving the environment in accordance with relevant provisions, the people's government shall provide support.

Article 24 The competent department of environmental protection of the people's government at or above the county level and the environmental monitoring institution entrusted by it, and other departments bearing the responsibility of environmental protection supervision and administration shall have the authority to conduct on-site inspection of enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators that discharge pollutants. The party under inspection shall truthfully report the situation and provide necessary materials. The department, institution, and its staff conducting on-site inspection shall keep trade secrets of the party under inspection.

Article 25 Where enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators discharge pollutants in violation of laws and regulations, causing or likely to cause serious pollution, the competent department of environmental protection of the people's government at or above the county level and other departments bearing the responsibility of environmental protection supervision and administration may seal up and seize the facilities and equipment causing pollutant discharge.

Article 26 The State shall implement the environmental protection target responsibility system and the assessment and evaluation system. The people's government at or above the county level shall incorporate the accomplishment of environmental protection targets into the assessment of the departments bearing the responsibility of environmental protection supervision and administration and their responsible persons of the people's government at the corresponding level and the people's government at the lower level and their responsible persons, as an important basis for assessment and evaluation. The assessment results shall be made public to the society.

Article 27 The people's government at or above the county level shall, on an annual basis, report to the people's congress at the corresponding level or its standing committee on the environmental situation and the accomplishment of environmental protection targets, and shall report to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level in a timely manner on the occurrence of major environmental incidents, and accept supervision according to law.

Article 28 Local people's governments at all levels shall, based on environmental protection targets and treatment tasks, adopt effective measures to improve environmental quality.
Where the relevant local people's governments of key regions and river basins fail to meet the national environmental quality standards, they shall formulate plans for achieving the standards within a prescribed time limit and take measures to meet the standards on schedule.

Article 29 The State shall delimit ecological protection red lines in key ecological function areas, ecologically sensitive and vulnerable areas, and other areas, and shall implement strict protection.
The people's governments at all levels shall take measures to protect various types of representative natural ecosystem areas, natural distribution areas of rare and endangered wild animals and plants, important water conservation areas, geological structures, famous caves, fossil distribution areas, glaciers, volcanoes, hot springs and other natural relics of significant scientific and cultural value, as well as cultural relics and ancient and famous trees, and shall strictly prohibit destruction.

Article 30 In the development and utilization of natural resources, rational development shall be carried out, biodiversity shall be protected, ecological security shall be ensured, and relevant plans for ecological protection and restoration and treatment shall be formulated and implemented according to law.
When introducing alien species and researching, developing, and utilizing biotechnology, measures shall be taken to prevent damage to biodiversity.

Article 31 The State shall establish and improve the ecological protection compensation system.
The State shall increase financial transfer payments to ecological protection areas. The relevant local people's governments shall ensure the allocation of ecological protection compensation funds and guarantee that they are used for ecological protection compensation.
The State shall guide the people's governments of beneficiary areas and ecological protection areas to conduct ecological protection compensation through consultation or in accordance with market rules.

Article 32 The State shall strengthen the protection of the atmosphere, water, soil, etc., and shall establish and improve the corresponding investigation, monitoring, assessment and remediation systems.

Article 33 The people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the protection of the agricultural environment, promote the use of new technologies for agricultural environmental protection, strengthen the monitoring and early warning of agricultural pollution sources, coordinate relevant departments to take measures to prevent and control soil pollution, land desertification, salinization, impoverishment, rocky desertification, land subsidence, and to prevent and control ecological imbalance phenomena such as vegetation damage, soil erosion, water eutrophication, water source depletion, and species extinction, and promote the comprehensive control of plant diseases and insect pests.
The people's governments at the county and township levels shall improve the public service level of rural environmental protection and promote the comprehensive improvement of the rural environment.

Article 34 The State Council and the local people's governments at all levels in coastal areas shall strengthen the protection of the marine environment. Discharging pollutants into the sea, dumping wastes, and constructing coastal engineering and marine engineering projects shall conform to the provisions of laws and regulations and relevant standards, and shall prevent and reduce pollution damage to the marine environment.

Article 35 Urban and rural construction shall take into account the characteristics of the local natural environment, protect vegetation, water areas and natural landscapes, and strengthen the construction and management of urban gardens, green spaces, and scenic spots and historic sites.

Article 36 The State shall encourage and guide citizens, legal persons, and other organizations to use products and recycled products that are conducive to environmental protection, and to reduce the generation of waste.
State organs and other organizations using fiscal funds shall give priority to the procurement and use of products, equipment, and facilities that are conducive to environmental protection, such as energy-saving, water-saving, and material-saving ones.
Article 37 Local people's governments at all levels shall take measures to organize the classified disposal, recycling, and utilization of domestic waste.

Article 38 Citizens shall abide by environmental protection laws and regulations, cooperate in the implementation of environmental protection measures, place domestic waste in a classified manner according to provisions, and reduce damage to the environment caused by daily life.

Article 39 The State shall establish and improve the monitoring, investigation, and risk assessment system for the environment and health; shall encourage and organize research on the impact of environmental quality on public health, and shall take measures to prevent and control diseases related to environmental pollution.

Article 40 The State shall promote cleaner production and resource recycling.
The relevant departments of the State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall take measures to promote the production and use of clean energy.
Enterprises shall give priority to the use of clean energy, adopt processes, equipment, and technologies for comprehensive utilization of waste and harmless treatment of pollutants with high resource utilization rates and low pollutant discharge, and reduce the generation of pollutants.

Article 41 The facilities for the prevention and control of pollution in a construction project shall be designed, constructed, and put into operation simultaneously with the main project. The facilities for the prevention and control of pollution shall comply with the requirements of the approved environmental impact assessment document and shall not be dismantled or left idle without authorization.

Article 42 Entities and other business operators that discharge pollutants shall take measures to prevent and control the pollution and harm to the environment caused by waste gas, wastewater, waste residues, medical waste, dust, malodorous gases, radioactive substances, as well as noise, vibration, light radiation, electromagnetic radiation, etc., generated in production, construction, or other activities.
Entities that discharge pollutants shall establish an environmental protection responsibility system and clearly define the responsibilities of the person in charge of the entity and relevant personnel.
Key pollutant-discharging entities shall install and use monitoring equipment in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and monitoring standards, ensure the normal operation of monitoring equipment, and preserve original monitoring records.
It is strictly prohibited to illegally discharge pollutants through concealed pipes, seepage wells, seepage pits, injection, or by tampering with or falsifying monitoring data, or by abnormal operation of pollution prevention facilities, or by other means that evade supervision.

Article 43 Entities and other business operators that discharge pollutants shall pay pollutant discharge fees in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. The pollutant discharge fees shall be entirely used specifically for the prevention and control of environmental pollution, and no entity or individual may intercept, divert, or misappropriate them for other purposes.
Where an environmental protection tax is levied in accordance with the provisions of law, no pollutant discharge fees shall be levied.

Article 44 The State implements a total emissions control system for key pollutants. The total emissions control indicators for key pollutants shall be issued by the State Council, and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall break them down and implement them. While implementing the national and local pollutant discharge standards, entities shall comply with the total emissions control indicators for key pollutants that are broken down and implemented for their unit.
For regions that exceed the national total emissions control indicators for key pollutants or fail to achieve the environmental quality targets set by the State, the competent departments of environmental protection under the people's governments at or above the provincial level shall suspend the approval of environmental impact assessment documents for construction projects that increase the total emissions of key pollutants.

Article 45 The State implements a pollutant discharge permit management system in accordance with the provisions of law.
Entities and other business operators that are subject to pollutant discharge permit management shall discharge pollutants in accordance with the requirements of the pollutant discharge permit; those that have not obtained a pollutant discharge permit shall not discharge pollutants.

Article 46 The State implements an elimination system for processes, equipment, and products that seriously pollute the environment. No entity or individual may produce, sell, or transfer or use processes, equipment, or products that seriously pollute the environment.
The introduction of technologies, equipment, materials, and products that do not comply with the environmental protection provisions of China is prohibited.

Article 47 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, as well as entities, shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China, properly carry out risk control, emergency preparedness, emergency response, and post-recovery work for environmental emergencies.
People's governments at or above the county level shall establish a public monitoring and early warning mechanism for environmental pollution and organize the formulation of early warning plans; when the environment is polluted and may affect public health and environmental safety, they shall timely release early warning information and initiate emergency measures according to law.
Entities shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, formulate emergency response plans for environmental emergencies, and report them to the competent department of environmental protection and relevant departments for record. When an environmental emergency occurs or is likely to occur, the entity shall immediately take measures to handle it, promptly notify units and residents that may be endangered, and report to the competent department of environmental protection and relevant departments.
After the emergency response to an environmental emergency is completed, the relevant people's government shall immediately organize an assessment of the environmental impact and losses caused by the incident, and timely publish the assessment results to the public.

Article 48 The production, storage, transportation, sale, use, and disposal of chemical substances and articles containing radioactive substances shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State to prevent environmental pollution.

Article 49 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments and institutions such as agriculture shall guide agricultural producers and operators in scientific planting and breeding, scientific and rational application of agricultural inputs such as pesticides and chemical fertilizers, and scientific disposal of agricultural wastes such as agricultural film and crop straw, to prevent agricultural non-point source pollution.
It is prohibited to apply solid wastes and wastewater that do not meet agricultural standards and environmental protection standards to farmland. When applying agricultural inputs such as pesticides and chemical fertilizers and conducting irrigation, measures shall be taken to prevent heavy metals and other toxic and hazardous substances from polluting the environment.
The site selection, construction, and management of livestock and poultry farms, breeding communities, and designated slaughtering enterprises shall comply with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations. Entities and individuals engaged in livestock and poultry breeding and slaughtering shall take measures to scientifically dispose of wastes such as livestock and poultry manure, carcasses, and sewage, to prevent environmental pollution.
People's governments at the county level shall be responsible for organizing the disposal of rural domestic waste.

Article 50 People's governments at all levels shall allocate funds in their fiscal budgets to support environmental protection work such as protection of rural drinking water sources, treatment of domestic sewage and other wastes, prevention and control of pollution from livestock and poultry breeding and slaughtering, soil pollution prevention and control, and treatment of pollution from rural industrial and mining enterprises.

Article 51 People's governments at all levels shall coordinate the construction of urban and rural sewage treatment facilities and supporting pipeline networks, environmental sanitation facilities for the collection, transportation, and disposal of solid wastes, centralized disposal facilities and sites for hazardous waste, and other public facilities for environmental protection, and shall ensure their normal operation.
Article 52 The State encourages the purchase of environmental pollution liability insurance.

Article 53 Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations shall, according to law, have the right to obtain environmental information, and to participate in and supervise environmental protection.
The competent departments of environmental protection of people's governments at all levels and other departments with environmental protection supervision and management responsibilities shall, according to law, disclose environmental information, improve public participation procedures, and facilitate participation in and supervision of environmental protection by citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.

Article 54 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall uniformly release national environmental quality, key pollution source monitoring information, and other major environmental information. The competent departments of environmental protection under the people's governments at or above the provincial level shall periodically release environmental status bulletins.
The competent departments of environmental protection under the people's governments at or above the county level and other departments with environmental protection supervision and management responsibilities shall, according to law, disclose information on environmental quality, environmental monitoring, environmental emergencies, as well as environmental administrative licenses, administrative penalties, and the collection and use of pollutant discharge fees.
The competent departments of environmental protection under the local people's governments at or above the county level and other departments with environmental protection supervision and management responsibilities shall record environmental violation information of entities and other business operators in the social credit file, and timely publish the list of violators to the public.

Article 55 Key pollutant-discharging entities shall truthfully disclose to the public the names of their major pollutants, discharge methods, discharge concentrations and total amounts, situations of excessive discharge, as well as the construction and operation of pollution prevention facilities, and shall accept public supervision.

Article 56 For a construction project for which an environmental impact report shall be prepared according to law, the construction entity shall, during the preparation, explain the situation to the public that may be affected and fully solicit opinions.
The department responsible for approving the environmental impact assessment document for a construction project shall, after receiving the environmental impact report for the construction project, fully disclose it except for matters involving State secrets or trade secrets; if it finds that the construction project has not fully solicited public opinions, it shall instruct the construction entity to solicit public opinions.

Article 57 Where citizens, legal persons, or other organizations discover that any entity or individual has engaged in acts of polluting the environment or damaging the ecosystem, they have the right to report to the competent department of environmental protection or other departments with environmental protection supervision and management responsibilities.
Where citizens, legal persons, or other organizations discover that local people's governments at all levels, the competent departments of environmental protection under the people's governments at or above the county level, or other departments with environmental protection supervision and management responsibilities have failed to perform their duties according to law, they have the right to report to their superior authorities or supervisory authorities.
The authority that accepts a report shall keep confidential the relevant information of the whistleblower and protect the lawful rights and interests of the whistleblower.

Article 58 For acts that pollute the environment, damage the ecosystem, and harm the public interest, social organizations that meet the following conditions may institute a prosecution with the People's Court:
(1) They are registered according to law with the civil affairs department of the people's government at or above the city with districts; and
(2) They have been specialized in environmental protection public interest activities for five consecutive years or more and have no record of illegal conduct.
Where a social organization that meets the provisions of the preceding paragraph institutes a prosecution with the People's Court, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.
A social organization that institutes a prosecution shall not seek economic benefits through the litigation.

Article 59 Where an entity or other business operator illegally discharges pollutants, is penalized with a fine, is ordered to make corrections, and refuses to do so, the administrative organ that made the penalty decision according to law may impose a daily consecutive penalty from the day following the date of the order for correction, based on the original amount of the fine.
The fine penalty provided for in the preceding paragraph shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations that stipulate the determination of the fine based on factors such as the operating cost of pollution prevention facilities, direct losses caused by the illegal act, or illegal gains.
Local regulations may, based on the actual needs of environmental protection, increase the types of illegal acts subject to daily consecutive penalties as provided for in the first paragraph.

Article 60 Where entities and other business operators discharge pollutants exceeding the pollutant discharge standards or exceeding the total emissions control indicators for key pollutants, the competent department of environmental protection under the people's government at or above the county level may order them to take measures such as restricting production or suspending production for remediation; if the circumstances are serious, it shall, upon approval by the people's government with approval authority, order the suspension of business or closure.

Article 61 Where a construction entity, without submitting the environmental impact assessment document for a construction project according to law or without obtaining approval for the environmental impact assessment document, commences construction without authorization, the department vested with the function of environmental protection supervision and administration shall order the cessation of construction, impose a fine, and may order restoration to the original state.

Article 62 Where, in violation of this Law, a key pollutant-discharging entity fails to disclose or fails to truthfully disclose environmental information, the environmental protection department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to disclose publicly, impose a fine, and make a public announcement.

Article 64 Where damage is caused by environmental pollution and ecological destruction, the tort liability shall be borne in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 65 Where an environmental impact assessment institution, an environmental monitoring institution, or an institution engaged in the maintenance and operation of environmental monitoring equipment and pollution prevention facilities, engages in fraud in relevant environmental service activities and bears responsibility for the environmental pollution and ecological destruction caused, in addition to being penalized in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations, it shall also bear joint and several liability together with other persons responsible for the environmental pollution and ecological destruction.

Article 66 The limitation period for bringing an action for compensation for environmental damage shall be three years, commencing from the time when the party knows or should have known that it has suffered damage.

Article 67 The people's government at a higher level and its environmental protection department shall strengthen supervision over the environmental protection work of the people's government at a lower level and its relevant departments. Where it finds that a relevant staff member has committed an illegal act for which a sanction shall be given according to law, it shall propose a sanction to the appointing and dismissing organ or the supervisory organ.
Where an administrative penalty shall be given according to law, but the relevant environmental protection department fails to impose such an administrative penalty, the environmental protection department of the people's government at a higher level may directly make a decision on administrative penalty.
Article 69 Where a violation of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 70 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2015.
